simple: A tuple is just a list of values passed or returned together, separated by commas. When the Roblox API reference says "Tuple", it means a function can take several values, or give several values back at once. Knowing this helps you read the API docs and catch every value a function returns.
analogy: A tuple is like a combo meal. You order one thing, but you get back a burger, fries, and a drink all at once. You can grab each item into its own hand (variable).
keyPoints: A tuple is a list of values, like `1, true, "hi"`.
If an API says a function takes a "Tuple", you can pass it many values, separated by commas.
`BindableFunction:Invoke()` takes a tuple, so `Invoke(1, true, "string", Vector3.new(0, 0, 0))` works.
If an API says a function returns a "Tuple", it gives back more than one value.
Catch multiple return values with multiple variables: `local content, isReady = Players:GetUserThumbnailAsync(...)`.

terms.tuple: Several values grouped together in order, separated by commas.
terms.parameter: A value a function asks for when you call it.
terms.argument: The actual value you pass to a function, like the `5` in `print(5)`.
terms.return value: A value a function gives back when it finishes.
terms.method: A function that belongs to an object, called with a colon, like `Players:GetPlayers()`.
terms.callback: A function you hand to something else so it can call it later.

example.title: Get a player's avatar picture
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	-- This method returns a tuple: two values at once
	local content, isReady = Players:GetUserThumbnailAsync(
		player.UserId,
		Enum.ThumbnailType.HeadShot,
		Enum.ThumbnailSize.Size420x420
	)
	print(player.Name, content, isReady)
end)
explain: When a player joins, the script asks for their headshot image.
`GetUserThumbnailAsync` returns two values: the image link and a true/false for whether it is ready.
`local content, isReady =` catches both values into two variables.
`print` shows the player's name, the image link, and whether it is ready.

watchOut: Only writing one variable, like `local content = ...`. You will silently lose the second value; add another variable to catch it.
Mixing up the order. The values come back in the order the API reference lists them.
